**Stable key:** `MEM-P03`  
**Difficulty:** **High**  
**Suggested label:** `difficulty:high` (metadata proposal; a title/body marker does not depend on label availability)  
**Planning baseline:** `Ozwasyd/FsusBlog@580cf1af614fd0edab9cb4c9ee95ec4e128b0327`  
**Acceptance predecessors:** `MEM-P02` (#3446)

### Objective

Make admission precede every controlled allocation and make the resulting ownership charge independently auditable across all participating resource domains.

### Source and scope precedence

This issue implements stage P03 of the user-supplied memory-governance report (version 1.0, 2026-09-15). The user's later requirement for default automatic discovery and activation supersedes `Preferred`, default-off, and mandatory manual-per-capability opt-in wording. Original work-item IDs are preserved for traceability. Baseline paths must be checked against the actual implementation candidate; this issue is not a claim that proposed types already exist.

### Mandatory policy and terminology

All configurable capabilities default to `Auto` when omitted. `Auto` means automatic discovery, bounded qualification, online activation, and deterministic selection for an eligible workload after resource admission. It does not mean indiscriminate allocation. A supported, release-qualified and runtime-qualified available path must not require a second enable flag, per-host approval file, or administrator confirmation. `Disabled` prevents new capability-specific probes and use, and drains existing owners before disposal. `Required` adds a strict requirement; it does not override safety, permissions, qualification, or budgets. The earlier report value `Preferred` is superseded, not an additional mode.

Detection, qualification, online state, effective path, and per-operation admission are separate facts. Unknown, Unsupported, NotVerified, Faulted, Disabled, and temporarily BudgetRejected are not synonyms. A missing signal is not zero usage. Qualifying a release/backend is not a manual opt-in on each deployment. The always-required accounting, ownership, and content-security rules are not optional capability switches.

### Scope and exclusions

No promise of exact RSS attribution or permanent physical-resource reservation is included. No removal of existing hard caps is permitted.

All product implementation introduced by this memory program remains C#/.NET. Supported already-installed OS/GPU APIs may be called through isolated C# adapters. Existing unrelated C++, frontend, protocol, and business components are not rewritten. Do not change AEDS/HTTP, authorization, revocation, publication, or delivery authority merely to simplify memory management.

### Files and ownership

| Status | Path or owner | Required treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| N | `src/backend/Infrastructure/Memory/Accounting/` | Resource ledger, reservation coordinator, tokens, and independent event observation. |
| B | `src/backend/Infrastructure/PublicReadArtifacts/PublicHotReadResidency.cs` | Adapt logical statistics without redefining their historical meaning. |
| B | `src/backend/Infrastructure/PublicAot/PublicAotBoundedMemoryCache.cs` | Expose existing limit/accounting integration points without removing hard limits. |
| N | `Memory accounting tests inside the existing backend test project` | Resolve exact test paths through current test ownership. |

B = baseline-reported; N = proposed-new; R = exact owner unresolved until MEM-P00. Paths and namespaces in this table are scope locators, not permission to create a parallel registry, publisher, scheduler, configuration source, or test runner. New tests must reside inside the actual owning project.

### Required implementation work

- [ ] **P03.1** Implement an allocation ledger keyed by unique AllocationId, with charged capacity, logical length, alignment slack, domain, owners, and state. Count shared physical allocations once and account for retained pool capacity without adding it twice. Snapshot metrics must not walk every blob on the request path.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P03-AC05`, `MEM-P03-AC06`, `MEM-P03-AC10`.
- [ ] **P03.2** Implement all-or-nothing resource-vector reservations with a documented linearization point. Check host, device, disk, subset, and operation-slot limits together. Do not hold a control lock during I/O or await another resource while keeping a partial reservation.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P03-AC01`, `MEM-P03-AC02`, `MEM-P03-AC09`.
- [ ] **P03.3** Implement reservation-to-allocation and ownership transfer without an uncharged intermediate state. Charge actual requested allocator capacity before allocation. If rounded or expanded capacity exceeds the original reservation, obtain the difference first or reject the allocation.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P03-AC03`, `MEM-P03-AC04`.
- [ ] **P03.4** Keep every live reservation and allocation charged across target reductions and policy reloads. Unstarted work may return its reservation; submitted work remains charged until safe completion. An obsolete policy revision must not make live tokens invisible.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P03-AC07`.
- [ ] **P03.5** Add observational accounting for existing managed allocations and pools. Distinguish requested length, rented bucket capacity, leased capacity, and retained capacity. Define clearing obligations for sensitive buffers without treating pool return as OS memory reclamation.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P03-AC05`, `MEM-P03-AC06`.
- [ ] **P03.6** Implement arithmetic, failure-injection, and concurrent-last-capacity tests. Cover invalid sizes, checked rounding, duplicate release, stale tokens, reservation conversion races, failure of any required domain, and shared-allocation reuse.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P03-AC01`, `MEM-P03-AC02`, `MEM-P03-AC03`, `MEM-P03-AC04`, `MEM-P03-AC07`, `MEM-P03-AC08`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **MEM-P03-AC01** Given a finite hard cap and concurrent attempts to spend its final available bytes, the sum of accepted unique allocation charges and unconsumed reservations never exceeds the cap. An independent event-log replay reaches the same total.
- [ ] **MEM-P03-AC02** If any required resource domain or slot is insufficient, the complete vector request fails and leaves no newly acquired charge or slot. Crossed host/device requests cannot deadlock by holding partial grants.
- [ ] **MEM-P03-AC03** A reservation conversion concurrent with a new request has no observable uncharged window. The total charge before and after conversion differs only by an explicitly admitted capacity adjustment.
- [ ] **MEM-P03-AC04** Zero, negative, overflowed, misaligned, or out-of-range requests are rejected before an allocator call. Failed allocation N returns only its own unspent reservation and preserves earlier sealed allocations.
- [ ] **MEM-P03-AC05** A shared block referenced by several generations contributes one physical charge. Role references, leases, pin/registration subsets, and logical representation bytes remain independently inspectable.
- [ ] **MEM-P03-AC06** Pool return ends the borrower lease but leaves retained capacity charged. A trim event removes charge only when the corresponding owner has actually relinquished that allocation to its allocator.
- [ ] **MEM-P03-AC07** After a budget reduction below live commitments, live commitments remain visible, new incompatible work is rejected, and over-target or infeasible state is emitted. No negative ledger value or token reuse is accepted.
- [ ] **MEM-P03-AC08** Correctness violations such as underflow, owner mismatch, and duplicate allocation identity stop the affected operation/backend and produce bounded evidence. They are not translated into an ordinary cache miss.
- [ ] **MEM-P03-AC09** Probe allocations and recovery operations use this same coordinator, with dedicated finite probe budgets. Automatic activation cannot allocate outside the ledger merely because it is initialization.
- [ ] **MEM-P03-AC10** Steady-state ledger observations use bounded memory and low-cardinality metrics. Neither observations nor admission introduce file, driver, database, or Redis access into an L0 hit.

### Required validation scope

Deterministic ledger/reservation tests and managed or injected-allocator observations. Real native allocation failure is independently required in MEM-P05.

| Scenario | Responsibility in this issue | Required observable assertion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `T01`: Concurrent requests for the final host budget | Primary implementation owner | Accepted unique charges plus unconsumed reservations never exceed the configured hard gate; failed requests leave no partial grant. |
| `T02`: Host capacity available but device or disk capacity insufficient | Primary implementation owner | The complete resource vector fails without partial ownership, leaked slots, or crossed-resource deadlock. |
| `T03`: Reservation conversion races with a new admission | Primary implementation owner | There is no uncharged conversion window; actual capacity rather than logical length is charged. |
| `T04`: Budget revision drops below live reservations | Primary implementation owner | Live charge remains visible, incompatible growth stops, and over-target/Infeasible is reported without fabricated release. |
| `T05`: Invalid, extreme, aligned, multiplied, or offset sizes | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P05 | Reject invalid or overflowing arithmetic before allocation and memory access; never wrap a large request into a small allocation. |
| `T06`: Allocator fails on allocation N | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P05 | Clean only the candidate-owned resources; earlier sealed data remains valid and outstanding accounting is correct. |
| `T07`: Several generations or variants share one block | Primary implementation owner | Charge the allocation once and explain separate role/reader references; retain it until all actual holds end. |
| `T08`: Pool rent, return, retention, and trim | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P14 | Lease return is distinct from retained ownership and OS reclamation; retained capacity stays charged. |
| `T13`: Repeated disposal, ownership misuse, and outstanding pins | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P04 | Release is idempotent or rejected explicitly; no underflow, double free, or stale-token/ABA reuse. |
| `T53`: Continuous pressure events and diagnostics | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P20 | Bound buffers, log volume, and label cardinality and prevent private-data disclosure. |

### Evidence and acceptance rules

Every unchecked acceptance criterion below is mandatory. `must` and `must not` are normative; `may` grants an option only where it is explicitly stated. A required test passes only when its specified assertion is observed on the current candidate. A comment stating that an assertion is true is not evidence.

Bind evidence to the actual commit and worktree fingerprint, fixture, toolchain, configuration revision, backend, OS/architecture, relevant driver/device identity, actual command, and raw result. Use the existing test DAG, required static admission, fixture ownership, and independent verifiers. All numeric limits and performance expressions referenced by this issue must be finite, explicit, and frozen by their owning policy/baseline before candidate results are examined. Missing values block acceptance; do not invent a passing threshold afterward.

Expected resource rejection must not conceal use-after-free, bounds violations, double free, uninitialized disclosure, revoked/wrong content, negative accounting, a parallel authority, or an unbounded queue. Any such correctness failure blocks acceptance regardless of performance. Do not rewrite frozen receipts or weaken tests. Missing platform or hardware evidence is `NotVerified`, not `Passed` or a convenient `NotApplicable`.

Evidence level is stage-specific: contract or fixture work may run before a downstream backend exists, but it does not certify that backend. Each primary implementation owner must supply its own required integration/platform evidence; MEM-P19 independently closes the complete matrix. Passing tests never authorizes automatic closure of this issue, another issue, or a pull request.

### Safe disable and rollback

A diagnostic shadow mode may stop new enforcement experiments, but existing hard limits and live charges remain intact. Live allocations cannot be erased from accounting during rollback.

### Completion report

Report the exact scope and files changed, every acceptance-criterion result, tests and commands actually run, raw current-source evidence, default Auto behavior, negative/competition cases, performance against frozen gates where applicable, unresolved support rows, and rollback results. A missing required environment leaves the corresponding promise unverified. Do not describe planned tests or a passing document validator as product verification.

Docker-related tests are not to be executed by this delivery agent under the project restriction. State them explicitly as not run. A Docker-specific assertion requires evidence from its authorized owner; a genuinely technology-independent assertion may use authorized non-Docker isolation. Do not fetch missing implementation dependencies from the network; record exact package/version/target gaps and stop the blocked execution item.

This increment implements managed capacity admission, bounded root/role/read/pin/actual-operation ownership, independent outer cancellation, exact drain and full-capacity clearing before charge release. CLR-invalid sizes reject before admission. It also implements portable GC/process/canonical-ledger pressure observations, bounded trace retention and deterministic normalization. Last-GC snapshots cannot supply an instantaneous rate; old domain revisions, missing/stale observations, reset counters and discontinuous clocks are refused.
